rows: You do not have to move faster. You have to move sooner.
Brawling is a fine habit when it has a purpose. I want to see yours.
Nerve is a timing error you choose in advance. Choose it sooner, not later.
Pace is not ability. I have seen fast people go nowhere.
The people deserve matcraft they can see. I will show them the sooner part.
I have seen the craft, and it starts earlier than you think.
I am still in the room. I still know the craft.
Look at the stance, and tell me what you see. It is ready early. That is the point.
Technique, in your words. Let us look at it. Correct me if I am wrong, but the hold begins before the grip.
Strikes are a late move in most matches. Start earlier.
A gamble taken late is a mistake. Take it sooner or not at all.
A stall is a misunderstanding about pace. Let me correct it.
The people want to see the craft. Give them the early moves.
You say you are among the best. The timing says otherwise. You still have the timing to learn.
You are proud of your {strength}. It is a fine start, but late. It is a fine start. You are late with the second half.
I have watched your {strength}, and it begins a moment too late.
You are composed. Good, that helps the timing. Well judged, that. Calm helps you move sooner, if you let it.
Noted. That is the correction I was going to make.
I could lecture you about that. Instead I will let you find it.
One fall, correctly timed. Keep me down, and you will have moved sooner than I did.
On the mat, move before I have finished the thought. Then we will both see.
Grounded or standing, the early move is the one that counts.
Keep facing me. Move before you are told.
That answer is in the right place. You moved sooner than I expected.
Still no answer. The timing is slipping. Take the earlier step, and answer.
Understood. We will correct the rest at the bell.
I will move early in this match, and I will not wait to be asked.
My approach is patient but early. You will see it when the timing matters.
Whatever happens, the early move will decide it.
We are not finished with the correction. There is still a sooner move to make.
I have one correction left, and you will see it when the bell rings.
I spoke a moment too soon. I cannot give you the example that would justify it.
The correction is mine to make. I haven't established the charge, so I won't carry it into the match.
Well judged. You corrected it before it became the whole argument.
Good. Save your timing for the contest now.
Watch which of us recognises the opening before the other moves. That is something the match can establish.
Look at the preparation for each hold, not merely the speed of its execution. You will see the difference.
Set the accusation aside. What can the people see about our craft from the first exchange?
The proof of a hold begins before the grip. What can we demonstrate through the wrestling itself?
Your preparation for my {strength} will count for something if you recognise the opening early enough. That is the part I shall test.
You know how to meet my {strength} once the exchange starts. Watch what happens a moment before that.
